Lessons.Title: Subtract Strategically
ExplanationParagraphs: Subtract Strategically: apply either a reliable subtraction algorithm or a more efficient representation according to the values, within 1,000. The original lesson also prepares for future multiplication through a separate Number Talk: Threes.

Warm-up — Number Talk: Threes, 10 minutes: calculate 2×6=12, 3×6=18, 2×7=14 and 3×7=21 mentally. Explain that 3 groups can be thought of as 2 groups plus 1 more group. This Number Talk is about multiplication, not subtraction, and must not be silently replaced with subtraction problems.

Activity 1 — How Would You Subtract?, 20 minutes: students choose algorithms or alternative strategies for these exact original five expressions: 451−329=122, 382−190=192, 924−285=639, 600−478=122 and 505−417=88. Organize each solution so peers can follow it.

Compare 382−190 using 382−200+10=192: compensation can be efficient because 190 is near 200. Compare 600−478 using count-on: 478→480 (+2), 480→600 (+120), difference 122. An algorithm remains correct; partners explain what makes a strategy useful for given addends.

With 451−329, ones 1 cannot subtract 9: exchange a ten, then 11−9=2, tens 4−2=2, hundreds 4−3=1, giving 122. For 924−285, tens 2 cannot subtract 8 tens: exchange a hundred; then ones 4 cannot subtract 5 ones: exchange a ten; obtain 639. For 505−417, a zero in the tens requires exchanging a hundred, then a ten; obtain 88.

Students first work independently; partners compare a method they both used, then a method that differs. MLR8 Discussion Supports encourages asking 'Can you say more about...?' and 'Why did you...?' Their discourse cannot be certified from a numeric response.

Activity 2 — Greatest Difference, Smallest Difference, 15 minutes: students work in pairs with the original 2021 paperclip spinner and recording sheet. Choose which kind of difference to make, alternate spins and assign digit to a place in each three-digit number, then calculate and compare the differences using >, < or =; replay and adjust place values deliberately.

The original six-page student PDF includes game recording sheets on pages 4 and 5 with side-by-side three-digit blanks for each player and their differences; an independent first-party blank table is provided. The publisher's original spinner should be teacher-supplied; do not invent claimed official spinner digits. For teacher synthesis compare 601 and 398: count on 398→400 (+2), 400→600 (+200), 600→601 (+1), giving 203.

Lesson synthesis: choose algorithm when composition is harder mentally; choose near-hundred compensation or count-on when the structure makes it efficient. The final source section summary reviews subtraction algorithms and strategy choice. Original publisher game artwork is not copied, and the gated Cool-down is not reproduced; independent Edulytics 505−417=88 assesses the same subtraction goal with teacher review.

KeyConcepts.Title: Strategic subtraction
KeyConcepts.Definition: The best method may be a written algorithm, counting on or subtracting compatible numbers.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Choose a method based on the numbers, justify it, and check the exact difference.

KeyConcepts.Title: Counting on
KeyConcepts.Definition: A difference can be measured by forward jumps from the smaller number to the larger number.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Sum only the increments from the subtrahend to the minuend.

KeyConcepts.Title: Place-value exchanges
KeyConcepts.Definition: When a place cannot be subtracted, exchange a higher unit without altering the total.
KeyConcepts.Example: 505−417=88 after composing a ten and then ones.

KeyConcepts.Title: Digit-position game
KeyConcepts.Definition: Choosing where spinner digits go affects the value of a three-digit number and the difference.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use the actual source spinner with a partner, then compare computed differences using >,<,=.
KeyConcepts.Example: For sample 601 and398, the exact difference is203.

WorkedExamples.Title: Near a multiple of a hundred
WorkedExamples.Question: Compute 382−190.
WorkedExamples.Method: Subtract a friendly 200, then correct by 10.
Steps: You subtracted 10 too many because 190 is ten less than 200.

WorkedExamples.Title: Count on from a near-hundred number
WorkedExamples.Question: Compute 600−478.

WorkedExamples.Title: Across a zero in the tens place
WorkedExamples.Question: Compute 505−417.
WorkedExamples.Method: Exchange a hundred into tens and one of the tens into ones.
Steps: Exchange:4 hundreds,10 tens,5 ones then4 hundreds,9 tens,15 ones.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The original 2021 Number Talk Threes computes four products as a bridge to later multiplication.
182 is the result of subtracting 200 rather than190.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating 600−478 as minus 478 with no regrouping.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Without exchanging hundreds and tens the written columns can yield impossible place values.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use a correct algorithm or count-on:478→480→600=122.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming the greatest possible difference is the same for every spinner.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The original source requires using the actual spinner results and placing the digits deliberately.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher checks chosen digit positions and subsequent difference.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Auto-marking partner participation from a game answer.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The original uses partner turns and comparisons with number records.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher reviews rounds and comparisons separately.

SummaryPoints: Five source subtraction answers in order:122,192,639,122,88.
Choose between a place-value algorithm and a flexible strategy.
Source game requires spinner-based number construction, comparison and at least one repeated round.
Original source section summary reviews the choice of subtraction strategy; independent Cool-down 505−417=88 is not the publisher's gated prompt.
